Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at Example 1 (2024-11-14):
- History: prices have been range 61-68, recently around 66-67
- Sentiment: varies from negative to positive, mostly low positivity
- Model forecasts: start around 68.12 and gradually decline to ~65.33
- True outcomes: start around 68.27 and gradually decline to ~71.56 (higher than forecasts!)

Wait, let me look more carefully. The model forecasts are lower than true outcomes in Example 1. The model starts at 68.12 but true outcomes start at 68.27. By day 30, model is at 65.96 but true outcomes are at 71.56 - that's a huge divergence!

Actually wait, let me re-read. Example 1 has date 2024-11-14 but the true outcomes end at 71.56. That seems very different from the starting forecasts of 68.12.

Let me look at Example 4 (2025-04-29):
- History: prices have been declining from 69.86 down to 65.31
- Sentiment: starts positive (1.00) then becomes mixed
- Model forecasts: start at 64.15 and gradually increase to 66.24
- True outcomes: start at 64.85 and gradually increase to 74.23

The model is significantly too low compared to true outcomes in Example 4. The model peaks at 66.24 while true outcomes peak at 74.23 - that's an 8-point difference!

Example 5 (2025-04-28) is very similar to Example 4 with the same error pattern.

Example 2 (2025-05-05):
- History: prices have been rising from 60.94 to 68.76


- Sentiment: mixed positivity
- Model forecasts: start at 67.47 and gradually increase to 70.67
- True outcomes: start at 67.47 and gradually increase to 75.94

I notice a consistent pattern of model forecasts being substantially lower than true outcomes across multiple examples. The divergence appears to be systematic, with true outcomes consistently outperforming model predictions by 4-10 points in the early days and up to 10+ points in later days.
